summary: A woman who traveled with her husband and came back saying he died is believed and may remarry, if there was peace at home and in the world. Rabbi Yehudah adds that she must come crying with torn clothes, but the Sages disagree.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: A woman who went with her husband overseas,
chunks.st: With regard to a woman who went, she and her husband, overseas, if there was

chunks.en: when there was peace between them and peace in the world,
chunks.st: peace between him and her, i.e., the couple were not fighting at the time, and there was also peace in the world, i.e., there was no war at that time,

chunks.en: and she came back and said,
chunks.st: and the woman came back by herself and said:

chunks.en: "My husband died,"
chunks.st: My husband died,

chunks.en: she may marry. "My husband died,"
chunks.st: she may marry on the basis of her own testimony. Likewise, if she said: My husband died, and they did not have children, but her husband had a brother,

chunks.he: תִּתְיַבֵּם. שָׁלוֹם בֵּינוֹ לְבֵינָהּ וּמִלְחָמָה בָעוֹלָם,
chunks.en: she may do yibum. Peace between them but war in the world,
chunks.explain: In a war, she may think he died when he did not.
chunks.st: she may enter into levirate marriage. If there was peace between him and her when they left but there was war in the world,

chunks.en: a fight between them but peace in the world,
chunks.st: or if there was a quarrel between him and her and peace in the world,

chunks.en: and she came back and said,
chunks.st: and she came and said:

chunks.en: "My husband died,"
chunks.st: My husband died,

chunks.en: she is not believed.
chunks.st: she is not deemed credible, as she may be mistaken or lying.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: she is never believed,
chunks.st: She is never deemed credible when she testifies that her husband died,

chunks.en: unless she came
chunks.st: unless she came

chunks.en: crying with her clothes torn.
chunks.st: crying and her clothing was torn, in which case it is apparent that she is speaking the truth.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to him: This is an incorrect distinction. Rather,

chunks.en: "Either way, she may marry."
chunks.st: both this woman who cries and this woman who does not cry may marry on the basis of their own testimony.

summary: Beis Hillel first said she is believed only if she came back from the grain harvest, like the story that happened. Beis Shammai said it is the same for any trip, and Beis Hillel agreed.

chunks.en: Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel say:

chunks.he: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ אֶלָּא בְּבָאָה מִן הַקָּצִיר,
chunks.en: "We only heard it about a woman coming from the harvest,
chunks.st: We heard that one may accept the testimony of a woman concerning the death of her husband only when she comes from the grain harvest,

chunks.en: and in that same country,
chunks.st: and when she testified in the same country where he died,

chunks.en: and like the story that happened."
chunks.st: and in circumstances similar to the incident that occurred, in which a lenient ruling was issued, as will be explained.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel: The same halakha applies to a wife

chunks.en: "Whether she comes from the grain harvest,
chunks.st: who comes from the grain harvest, and

chunks.en: or comes from the olives,
chunks.st: one who comes from the olive harvest,

chunks.en: or comes from the grape harvest,
chunks.st: and also one who comes from the grape harvest,

chunks.en: or comes from one country to another.
chunks.st: and even one who comes from one country to another country. Although the incident in question took place during the grain harvest,

chunks.he: לֹא דִבְּרוּ חֲכָמִים בַּקָּצִיר אֶלָּא בַהֹוֶה.
chunks.en: The Sages spoke of the harvest only because that is what happened."
chunks.st: the Sages spoke of the grain harvest only because it was the present occurrence, i.e., that is what happened in practice, but this is no proof that she is deemed credible only when she arrived specifically from the grain harvest. The mishna comments:

chunks.he: חָזְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּבֵית שַׁמָּאי:
chunks.en: Beis Hillel changed their mind and taught like Beis Shammai.
chunks.st: Beit Hillel retracted their opinion, and decided to teach in accordance with the opinion of Beit Shammai on this issue.

summary: Beis Shammai say a woman who is believed that her husband died also gets her kesubah. Beis Hillel first argued, but they changed their mind and agreed.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say: A woman who testifies that her husband died

chunks.en: "She may marry and take her kesubah."
chunks.st: may marry, and take the money guaranteed in her marriage contract.

chunks.en: Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: "She may marry, but not take her kesubah."
chunks.st: She may marry, but she may not take her marriage contract, as qualified witnesses are required for monetary matters.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai said to them: If

chunks.en: "You allowed a serious matter of a forbidden marriage;
chunks.st: you have permitted a woman potentially forbidden to him, which is a relatively stringent prohibition, based merely upon her own testimony,

chunks.en: will you not allow a light matter of money?"
chunks.st: will we not permit a monetary matter, which is more lenient, as the money can be returned and this sin does not entail such a severe punishment?

chunks.en: Beis Hillel said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel said to them: This is no proof, as

chunks.en: "We see that the brothers do not take
chunks.st: we find that the brothers do not come into the

chunks.en: the inheritance because of her word."
chunks.st: inheritance from the deceased brother based on her testimony.
chunks.stMore: Evidently, although this testimony is accepted with regard to forbidden sexual relationships, it is not effective for monetary matters.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai said to them:

chunks.en: "We can learn from her kesubah document,
chunks.st: But we can learn this halakha from the scroll of the marriage contract,

chunks.en: which he writes for her:
chunks.st: as every husband writes for her that:

chunks.en: 'If you marry another man,
chunks.st: If you marry another man,

chunks.en: take what is written for you.'"
chunks.st: take what is written for you in this contract.
chunks.stMore: This shows that her right to receive the money of her marriage contract is dependent upon her eligibility to remarry. In this case, as she is deemed credible when she says her husband died and she may marry again, she is likewise entitled to the money of the marriage contract.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel changed their mind and taught
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel again retracted their opinion, and decided to teach

chunks.en: like Beis Shammai.
chunks.st: in accordance with the opinion of Beit Shammai.

summary: Everyone is believed to say a woman's husband died, except some women who may dislike her. The mishnah also teaches what happens when witnesses disagree.

chunks.en: Everyone is believed to tell her,
chunks.st: All are deemed credible when they come to give testimony with regard to the death of a woman’s husband,

chunks.en: except her mother-in-law,
chunks.st: apart from her mother-in-law,

chunks.en: her mother-in-law's daughter,
chunks.st: the daughter of her mother-in-law,

chunks.en: her co-wife, her sister-in-law,
chunks.st: her rival wife, the wife of her yavam,

chunks.en: and her husband's daughter.
chunks.explain: These women may not like her, so they might lie.
chunks.st: and her husband’s daughter, her stepdaughter. The reason is that these women are likely to hate her and will lie to her detriment.

chunks.en: What is the difference between a get and a death?
chunks.st: The mishna explains: In the case of a divorce all people, including these women, may bring her bill of divorce and testify that it was written appropriately. What, then, is the difference between a bill of divorce and death? The mishna answers: The difference is that in the case of a bill of divorce

chunks.en: The writing proves it.
chunks.st: the writing proves the accuracy of the testimony, i.e., her testimony is supported by the text of the document itself, whereas with regard to the death of her husband there is no proof apart from the statement of the woman herself.

chunks.en: If one witness says he died,
chunks.st: If one witness says: The man died,

chunks.he: וְנִשֵּׂאת, וּבָא אַחֵר וְאָמַר לֹא מֵת,
chunks.en: and she married, and another came and said he did not die,
chunks.st: and the wife married based on this testimony, and one other witness came and said: He did not die,

chunks.en: she does not have to leave.
chunks.st: she need not leave her new husband due to this testimony.

chunks.en: If one witness says he died,
chunks.st: However, if one witness comes and says: The husband died,

chunks.en: and two say he did not die,
chunks.st: and two witnesses say: He did not die, then

chunks.en: even though she married,
chunks.st: even though she married based on the first witness

chunks.en: she must leave. If two say he died,
chunks.st: she must leave her new husband. If two witnesses say: He died,

chunks.en: and one witness says he did not die,
chunks.st: and one witness says: He did not die, the testimony of the two witnesses is accepted, and

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִשֵּׂאת, תִּנָּשֵׂא:
chunks.en: even though she has not married, she may marry.
chunks.st: even though she did not yet marry, she may marry.

summary: When two wives of the same man disagree about whether he died, each is treated by her own words. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah argue when they disagree about how he died.

chunks.en: One wife says he died, and one
chunks.st: If two women who were married to the same man come forward, and one of them says that the husband died, and

chunks.en: says he did not die:
chunks.st: the other one says he did not die,

chunks.he: זוֹ שֶׁאוֹמֶרֶת מֵת תִּנָּשֵׂא וְתִטֹּל כְּתֻבָּתָהּ.
chunks.en: the one who says he died may marry and take her kesubah,
chunks.st: the one who says he died may marry on the basis of her own testimony, and she takes the money of her marriage contract.

chunks.en: and the one who says he did not die may not
chunks.st: And the one who said he did not die

chunks.en: marry, and does not take her kesubah.
chunks.st: may not marry, and does not take the money of her marriage contract. If

chunks.he: אַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת מֵת וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת נֶהֱרָג,
chunks.en: If one says he died and one says he was killed,
chunks.st: one wife says: He died in a normal manner, and the other one says: He was killed,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: "Since they say different things,
chunks.st: Since they contradict one another,

chunks.en: they may not marry."
chunks.st: these women may not marry.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Shimon say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon say:

chunks.he: הוֹאִיל וְזוֹ וָזוֹ מוֹדוֹת שֶׁאֵינוֹ קַיָּם,
chunks.en: "Since both agree he is not alive,
chunks.st: Since they both agree that he is not alive

chunks.en: they may marry." If one witness says he died and one witness
chunks.st: they may marry, despite the fact that they dispute the circumstances of his demise. If a witness says: He died, and a witness says:

chunks.en: says he did not die,
chunks.st: He did not die,

chunks.en: or one woman says he died and one woman
chunks.st: or one woman says: He died, and another

chunks.en: says he did not die,
chunks.st: woman says: He did not die,

chunks.en: she may not marry.
chunks.st: this woman may not marry.

summary: A woman who says her husband died may remarry, but her co-wife may not rely on her. Rabbi Tarfon lets the co-wife still eat terumah; Rabbi Akiva says she may neither remarry nor eat terumah.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: A woman who went with her husband overseas,
chunks.st: In the case of a woman who went, she and her husband, overseas,

chunks.en: and came back and said, "My husband died,"
chunks.st: and she comes and says: My husband died,

chunks.en: may marry and take her kesubah,
chunks.st: she may marry, and she takes her marriage contract based on her own testimony.

chunks.en: but her co-wife is forbidden.
chunks.explain: A co-wife is not believed about the other wife.
chunks.st: And it remains prohibited for her rival wife to remarry, as a woman cannot testify on behalf of her rival wife.

chunks.en: If she was a Jewish woman married to a Kohen,
chunks.st: If the rival wife was an Israelite woman married to a priest,

chunks.en: she may eat terumah.
chunks.st: she may continue to partake of teruma, as she is not permitted to remarry, and therefore the presumption that the husband is still alive is maintained in relation to her. This is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Tarfon says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Tarfon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.he: אֵין זוֹ דֶרֶךְ מוֹצִיאַתָּה מִידֵי עֲבֵרָה,
chunks.en: "This is not the way to keep her from sin,
chunks.st: This is not the way to spare someone from transgression.
chunks.stMore: According to the opinion of Rabbi Tarfon, there is a concern that she might be eating teruma unlawfully. There is no remedy for this situation

chunks.en: unless she is forbidden to marry
chunks.st: unless it is prohibited for the rival wife to marry, as she cannot rely on the testimony of her rival wife,

chunks.en: and forbidden to eat terumah."
chunks.st: and it is also prohibited for her to partake of teruma, lest the other woman was speaking the truth. In other words, the halakha is stringent on both counts.

summary: More arguments between Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva about avoiding sin: about a mother-in-law, about a man who married one of five women and does not know which, and about a man who stole from one of five people.

chunks.en: If she said, "My husband died, and after
chunks.st: The mishna discusses a similar case. If a woman said:

chunks.en: that my father-in-law died,"
chunks.st: My husband died and afterward my father-in-law died,

chunks.en: she may marry and take her kesubah,
chunks.st: she may marry and take her marriage contract,

chunks.en: but her mother-in-law is forbidden.
chunks.st: and it is prohibited for her mother-in-law to remarry, as a woman may not testify on behalf of her mother-in-law.

chunks.en: If she was a Jewish woman married to a Kohen,
chunks.st: If the mother-in-law was the daughter of an Israelite married to a priest,

chunks.en: she may eat terumah.
chunks.st: she may partake of teruma;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Tarfon says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Tarfon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.he: אֵין זוֹ דֶרֶךְ מוֹצִיאַתָּה מִידֵי עֲבֵרָה,
chunks.en: "This is not the way to keep her from sin,
chunks.st: This is not the way to spare her from transgression; there is no remedy

chunks.en: unless she is forbidden to marry
chunks.st: unless it is prohibited for the mother-in-law to marry

chunks.en: and forbidden to eat terumah."
chunks.st: and also prohibited for her to partake of teruma.

chunks.en: If he made kiddushin with one of five women
chunks.st: In relation to the dispute between Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva in the previous mishna, in which Rabbi Akiva states that one must avoid a possible transgression, the mishna cites two similar cases involving other topics. With regard to one who betrothed one of five women,

chunks.en: and does not know which one,
chunks.st: and he does not know which of them he betrothed, and

chunks.en: and each one says, "He married me,"
chunks.st: each one of them says: He betrothed me, if he does not want to marry any of them

chunks.en: he gives a get to each one of them,
chunks.st: he gives a bill of divorce to each and every one of them so none will have the status of a woman with regard to whom there is uncertainty whether she is divorced.

chunks.en: and leaves one kesubah between them and goes away.
chunks.st: And he leaves the marriage contract among them and departs. The marriage contract remains in dispute between the women until they clarify which of them is entitled to the money. This is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Tarfon says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Tarfon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.he: אֵין זוֹ דֶרֶךְ מוֹצִיאַתּוּ מִידֵי עֲבֵרָה,
chunks.en: "This is not the way to keep him from sin,
chunks.st: This is not the way to spare someone from transgression, as perhaps the woman he actually betrothed will not receive the money to which she is entitled. There is no remedy

chunks.en: unless he gives a get and a kesubah
chunks.st: unless he gives a bill of divorce and a marriage contract payment

chunks.en: to each one of them."
chunks.st: to each and every one.

chunks.en: If he stole from one of five people and does not
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of one who stole money from one of five people

chunks.en: know from which one he stole,
chunks.st: and does not know from which of them he stole, and

chunks.en: and each one says, "He stole from me,"
chunks.st: each one says: He stole from me,

chunks.en: he leaves the stolen money between them and goes away.
chunks.st: he leaves the stolen money among them and departs, and they will decide among themselves how to distribute the money; this is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Tarfon says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Tarfon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.he: אֵין זוֹ דֶרֶךְ מוֹצִיאַתּוּ מִידֵי עֲבֵרָה,
chunks.en: "This is not the way to keep him from sin,
chunks.st: This is not the way to spare him from transgression; there is no remedy

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיְּשַׁלֵּם גְּזֵלָה לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד:
chunks.en: unless he pays back each one of them."
chunks.st: unless he pays each and every one of them.

summary: A woman traveled with her husband and son and came back alone. If she says her husband died first, she is believed and is free. If she says her son died first, she is not believed for yibum, so she does chalitzah.

chunks.en: A woman who went with her husband
chunks.st: In the case of a woman who went, she and her husband,

chunks.en: overseas, and her son was with them,
chunks.st: overseas, and her son was with them, and later

chunks.en: and she came back and said, "My husband died,
chunks.st: she came back and said: My husband died

chunks.en: and after that my son died,"
chunks.st: and afterward my son died,

chunks.he: נֶאֱמֶנֶת. מֵת בְּנִי וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בַּעְלִי,
chunks.en: she is believed. "My son died, and after that my husband died,"
chunks.st: she is deemed credible. It is permitted for her to remarry, and she is exempt from levirate marriage. The reason is that she had children when she left, and therefore she retains her presumptive status of one who is exempt from levirate marriage. However, if she said: My son died and afterward my husband died,

chunks.en: she is not believed.
chunks.st: she is not deemed credible, i.e., she may not enter into levirate marriage.

chunks.en: But we worry about her words,
chunks.st: And yet we are concerned and give some credence to her statement, in case she was actually widowed by a childless husband, and therefore

chunks.en: so she does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: she performs ḥalitza to exempt her from the levirate bond with her yavam, and she does not enter into levirate marriage.

summary: A woman says she had a son overseas. If she says the son died before her husband, she is believed. If she says her husband died first, she is not believed, but she still needs chalitzah.

chunks.en: "A son was born to me overseas,"
chunks.st: If she went with her childless husband and returned alone and testified: A son was born to me overseas,

chunks.en: and she said, "My son died, and after
chunks.st: and she further said: My son died

chunks.en: that my husband died,"
chunks.st: and afterward my husband died,

chunks.he: נֶאֱמֶנֶת. מֵת בַּעְלִי וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בְּנִי,
chunks.en: she is believed. "My husband died, and after that my son died,"
chunks.st: she is deemed credible and may even enter into levirate marriage, as she was presumed to be childless when she left and consequently she retains that presumptive status. However, if she said: My husband died and afterward my son died,

chunks.en: she is not believed.
chunks.st: she is not deemed credible for the purpose of exempting her from levirate marriage,

chunks.en: But we worry about her words,
chunks.st: but the court is concerned about her statement.

chunks.en: so she does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: And therefore she must perform ḥalitza and she does not enter into levirate marriage.

summary: A woman is believed about a brother-in-law born overseas. But if they all left together, she is not believed that the yavam died, and a person is not believed when his words would let him marry someone.

chunks.en: "A yavam was born to me overseas,"
chunks.st: If she said: A yavam was born for me overseas, i.e., when the family left the country her husband did not have a brother, and she claims that in the meantime a brother was born to her husband,

chunks.en: and she said, "My husband died, and after
chunks.st: and she also said: My husband died

chunks.en: that my yavam died,"
chunks.st: and afterward my yavam died, or:

chunks.en: or "my yavam, and after that my husband,"
chunks.st: My yavam died and afterward my husband died, in either case

chunks.he: נֶאֱמֶנֶת. הָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ וִיבָמָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: she is believed. If she, her husband, and her yavam went overseas,
chunks.st: she is deemed credible. This is because when she left she was not presumed to require levirate marriage, and the suggestion that her husband now has a brother is based solely on her testimony. However, if she went, she and her husband and her yavam, overseas, and upon her return she

chunks.en: and she said, "My husband died, and after
chunks.st: said: My husband died and afterward

chunks.en: that my yavam died,"
chunks.st: my yavam died, or:

chunks.en: or "my yavam, and after that my husband,"
chunks.st: My yavam died and afterward my husband died,

chunks.en: she is not believed.
chunks.st: she is not deemed credible, as

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין הָאִשָּׁה נֶאֱמֶנֶת לוֹמַר מֵת יְבָמִי,
chunks.en: A woman is not believed to say, "My yavam died,"
chunks.st: a woman is not deemed credible if she says: My yavam died, in order

chunks.en: so that she can marry. Nor,
chunks.st: that she may marry another man. And she is not deemed credible if she says that

chunks.en: "My sister died,"
chunks.st: her sister died, in order

chunks.en: so that she can marry her husband.
chunks.st: that she may enter the house of her sister’s husband.

chunks.he: וְאֵין הָאִישׁ נֶאֱמָן לוֹמַר מֵת אָחִי,
chunks.en: And a man is not believed to say, "My brother died,"
chunks.st: And a man is not deemed credible if he says: My brother died,

chunks.en: so that he can do yibum with his wife.
chunks.st: so that he may enter into levirate marriage with his brother’s wife,

chunks.en: Nor, "My wife died,"
chunks.st: and he is not deemed credible when he says that his wife died,

chunks.en: so that he can marry her sister.
chunks.st: in order that he may marry his wife’s sister. The Sages accepted impaired testimony of this kind only when there was a concern about creating a situation of a deserted wife.
